record.original_question: Can we see on the induced action φ if Φ is smoothable or not?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1. Can we see on the induced action φ if Φ is smoothable or not?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group and let $\Phi : G \to \mathrm{Homeo}_+(\mathbb{R}^2)$ be an action of $G$ on the plane by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms preserving a pair of transverse (topological) foliations $(\mathcal{F}^+, \mathcal{F}^-)$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$. Such an action canonically extends to an action $\varphi : G \to \mathrm{Homeo}_+(\mathbf{S}^1)$ on the circle at infinity associated to the bifoliated plane $(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathcal{F}^+, \mathcal{F}^-)$. Call $\Phi$ smoothable if it is topologically conjugate to an action of $G$ on $\mathbb{R}^2$ by $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms preserving a pair of transverse smooth foliations.

Question: Is there a property of the induced circle action $\varphi : G \to \mathrm{Homeo}_+(\mathbf{S}^1)$ that detects whether the bifoliated planar action $\Phi$ is smoothable? Equivalently, can smoothability of $\Phi$ be read off from $\varphi$ alone?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem in a 2024 problem list from a conference on foliations and diffeomorphism groups, posted in 2025. No subsequent work resolving whether smoothability of a bifoliated planar action can be detected from its induced circle-at-infinity action was found.
